absent: Full layouts of folio, vm_area_struct, vm_fault, userfaultfd_ctx, uffd_msg and hstate beyond fields observed in these fragments.
Implementations of fault lock helpers, VMA read locking, huge fault hash, page table walkers, marker predicates and reservation accounting called but not shown.
Userfault monitor protocol including poll and read wakeup, copy and zero resolution paths, and event queue handling outside the fault entry.
Huge page allocation, page cache insertion details, copy on write, migration interaction and error handling beyond the observed call sites.
Scheduler yielding, reference counting, wait queue, slab cache, inode size and block accounting internals referenced only as stubs.

findings.text: Provides a gigantic folio copy helper that iterates over a caller supplied page count, resolves each destination and source page within the folios, yields the scheduler between iterations, derives per page addresses from a hint aligned down to the destination folio extent, performs a machine check aware user copy tied to the given area, and signals hardware poison on failure versus success otherwise.

Exposes an operation that attaches an anonymous folio to the anonymous set of a given area, tagging the stored pointer as anonymous and publishing pointer plus tag together with an ordered single store so concurrent observers never see a partial update.

Initializes reverse mapping for a newly faulted private huge folio by confirming huge type and fault address inside the area, starting whole and large mapping counters at zero, clearing a restore reservation marker, linking the folio as anonymous at the fault location, and marking the head page as exclusively owned.

Requires releasing the area read lock and the hash selected huge fault mutex before delegating to the generic userfault path, because that path may sleep and may drop the address space lock, invalidating any area assumptions across the handoff.

Acts as the central userfault entry that rejects exiting or dumping tasks, asserts the fault lock is held, requires an attached context belonging to the faulting address space, enforces exactly one recognized reason flag, honors a bus error shortcut and a user mode only restriction, demands retry permission, and takes a nowait fast path that requests an immediate retry, otherwise defaulting to bus error.

Describes the sleep lifecycle once waiting is allowed: take a context reference, build a fault notification, choose a sleep state from fault flags, make the waiter visible on the pending queue under interrupt safe locking before setting task state, revalidate need through the huge or normal table check with appropriate area locking, drop the fault lock, wake pollers and sleep only while still needed and not released, then remove any residual queue linkage and release the reference.

Handles a concurrently observed release by proactively dropping the fault lock and returning a retry status, which lets a closing manager progress, avoids forcing bus errors on noncooperative managers, and avoids spinning without releasing the read lock in page pinning paths.

Manages context lifetime by reference counting where acquisition adds a reference and release drops one, freeing only on the final drop after asserting all pending, fault, event and poll queues are idle and unlocked, then releasing the address space reference and returning the object to its cache.
States that the userfault message occupies 32 bytes on the wire and is fully zeroed including padding to prevent disclosure of kernel memory.

Builds the fault notification by reporting a page fault event, selecting exact versus coalesced fault address according to feature, translating write access and write protect and read write protect and minor reasons into user visible flag bits, and optionally attaching the current thread identity.

Defines the huge recheck that locates the huge entry for the fault address at the area page size; missing table, empty entry or userfault marker means wait, while a swapped nonpresent entry means do not wait so migration can redeliver, with write protection and protection without access plus marker tested against the corresponding reasons and plain protection without marker excluded.

Defines the normal recheck that walks upper levels to middle and leaf entries without table locks; absent upper levels, empty middle or leaf entries, or userfault markers mean wait, nonpresent swap entries mean do not wait, with transparent huge and leaf writability and protection plus marker tested against the corresponding reasons and transient leaf mapping races retried.
Maps fault flags to sleep state by preferring interruptible when requested, else killable when requested, else uninterruptible by default.
Supplies a weak default for the area memory management page size that forwards to the kernel page size helper, permitting architecture specific override.
Provides a fallback huge recheck for builds without huge support that warns as unreachable and reports no waiting needed.

Serves as the missing huge page fault entry operating under area read protection and a hash selected fault mutex, resolving or allocating backing for the fault offset, installing a huge mapping that preserves write protect markers, optionally completing a private write copy within the same fault, and always releasing table, area and mutex resources while reporting retry, bus error, out of memory, poison or success.

Distinguishes shared backing inserted into the page cache from private backing locked as new anonymous folios, zeroes and marks fresh folios current, prechecks private write reservations outside the table lock with release on success and restoration on failure, accounts pages to the address space, and marks only newly allocated folios as migratable.

Enforces table stability by comparing the live huge entry under the huge table lock against the fault time snapshot and retrying without installing state on any change, revalidating stability before reporting userfault missing or minor events since false positives are acceptable but incorrect logical events are not.

Reports fault failures as bus error for reservation revoked state with rate limited notice, bus error for offsets beyond file size, poison with size index for poisoned folios, out of memory for failed private reservation, and allocation errors mapped to bus error or silent retry depending on whether the entry remained stable against concurrent migration.

Inserts a shared huge folio into the page cache by scaling the index by huge order, holding the folio locked across insertion with unlock on failure, clearing restore reservation on success, marking dirty to pin against ordinary reclaim, and updating block accounting under the inode lock.

Implements a stability probe that acquires the huge table lock for the target, compares the current entry with a supplied snapshot for equality, releases the lock, and returns the comparison for retry decisions.

Treats table rechecks as lockless wait checks that tolerate concurrent modification, explicitly avoiding write decoding on swap entries, requiring presence before protection tests, and handling changed or in flight entries via retry rather than installation.

Propagates memory errors by converting machine check copy failure during gigantic copy into hardware poison status and by refusing to install huge mappings for poisoned folios, ensuring faults on errored offsets do not silently succeed.

Observes a fault bundle carrying area, fault and exact addresses, access flags, file offset, table location with original snapshot plus table lock slot, and a wait bundle linking the sleeping task with its notification message, context reference and woken marker across pending and poll queues.
Requires the folio to be locked and the area to already own an anonymous set before retargeting anonymous reverse mapping, with verification traps on violation.
